newsitem.title: UK: Bhutto's husband says attacks on him aimed at her.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto's husband says attacks on him aimed at her.

text.p: The imprisoned husband of former Pakistan prime minister Benazir Bhutto has accused President Farooq Leghari of making corruption allegations against him in order to get at his wife, the BBC said on Friday.
It said that in an interview to be broadcast in Britain on Saturday, Asif Ali Zardari said: "They just have to attack somebody. They had to make a target and they have to build around it."
The BBC said Zardari, accused by Leghari of skimming off $1.5 million from the Pakistan economy in the three years his wife was in power, gave his first major interview since he was arrested.
Leghari dismissed Bhutto from the premiership in November, a decision endorsed this week by Pakistan's Supreme Court which found evidence against her of corruption, nepotism and misrule.
Pakistanis vote on Monday in new national assembly elections which polls indicate Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party is set to lose.

Zardari, who is awaiting trial on charges of conspiracy to murder Bhutto's brother, told the BBC in the interview that Leghari and government advisers had found it difficult to make people believe that there was "something wrong" with his wife.
"So who do they have to make believe that there is something wrong with her? It's the husband, because if you hit the husband, you're hitting home," he said.
Zardari said he was known for years in Pakistan business circles as "Mr Ten Percent", but that nothing had ever been proved against him.
